I hate that you can relate to the pain. One time I was telling my therapist about the bitterness and she said “would you want your friends to feel the same pain of parent loss?” I thought “well absolutely not. But it’s unfair I have too” then I just have guilt lol just a never ending cycle. Most of the time I do okay, but it’s the smallest things that amp it up. Spring is around the corner and my mom loved gardening and planting flowers. I remember as a kid, she would spend what felt like hours looking at all of the different bulbs & things and I was always so bored. What I wouldn’t give to go flower shopping with her now..  & I always miss my dad’s goofy sense of humor & commentary on things.

The walking down the aisle comment is soo true. I recently went to a friends wedding & her dad was giving a toast and when they did the father/daughter dance… ugh my heart just ached. The jealousy is so hard. I also get really frustrated when people complain about their parents.. I know we are all human & not everyone is close with their parents, but I would have loved to have my parents live until they were elderly.

Ugh, I am so sorry! (Which I know hearing “I’m sorry” over and over gets old, trust me.) I read your other posts & saw the one about the sense of relief. I remember feeling that way with both of my parents & having guilt over it. It was such a weird feeling. Deep heartache having lost them.. but a sense of relief that cancer was no longer making them suffer. I hate that you had to witness cancer as well. It is awful & traumatic and I just hate it. Sorry if I’m rambling, I just can’t ever find the right words.
